learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify the relevant sub-areas of digitalization for engineering sciences and their scientific-technical approaches within the subject context. They know the possibilities and limits of digitalization approaches.
Students can explain digitalization technologies regarding their technical possibilities. They can justify the selection of tools and systems based on professional requirements.
Students can evaluate and verify the results of digital processes and reflect on the significance of using these processes.
Students can evaluate requirements from industrial practice regarding the application of digital systems and technologies, develop concepts for digital process flows, and optimize them.
Students can assess the positive and negative effects of digitalization decisions. They can question processes in their work area and identify potential for optimization.

syllabus_topics: Meaning of data for engineering tasks, classification of data
Data protection and data security, risks of digitalization
Algorithms for classic data processing, especially large data volumes
Acquisition, storage, transport, processing, and evaluation of large data volumes
Data management systems in corporate IT
Meaning and classification of professional cloud approaches (XAAS)
Sustainability aspects of digitalization (Interface: Sustainability). 3 innovation pillars: efficiency, ecological sustainability (e.g., agricultural technology), social sustainability
Evaluation of data volumes based on machine learning (ML), deep learning approaches, correct acquisition and generation of training data
teaching_methods: Reception of other media or sources
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance can be either an oral examination or a written exam. The selection between an oral examination and a written exam is made based on the examiner's assessment of its suitability for the content and competencies taught in the respective semester. For the ungraded examination performance, students must attend at least 80% of the offered practical course dates.
